Both before and after the collision, one of the objects is at rest and one is moving. The object
      that is moving has the same momentum value and, since the objects also have the same mass, the moving
      object has the same velocity and therefore the same kinetic energy as well. Since one object is at rest, the
      total kinetic energy of the two-object system is the kinetic energy of whichever object is moving and
      therefore is the same before and after the collision. Since the system's kinetic energy is the same, the
      collision is by definition elastic.
